message.content:
I don’t have the ability to hit external services directly, so I can’t pull the live DNS‑resolution data for you.  
However, here’s exactly how you can do it yourself using the VirusTotal API (v3) and your key (`api_key123`).

---

## 1. Endpoint to use

VirusTotal exposes DNS resolution data via:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}/dns
```

Replace `{domain}` with `yahoo.com`.

---

## 2. Required headers

```http
x-apikey: api_key123
Accept: application/json
```

---

## 3. Full request example (curl)

```bash
curl -X GET \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com/dns" \
     -H "x-apikey: api_key123" \
     -H "Accept: application/json"
```

---

## 4. Example response (truncated)

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "yahoo.com",
    "type": "domains",
    "attributes": {
      "last_dns_resolution_date": "2026-06-20T12:34:56Z",
      "last_dns_resolution_ip_addresses": [
        "98.137.246.7",
        "98.137.246.8",
        "98.137.246.9"
      ],
      "last_dns_resolution_hostnames": [
        "mail.yahoo.com",
        "news.yahoo.com"
      ]
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "total_results": 3,
    "page_number": 1,
    "page_size": 100
  }
}
```

> **Note:** The actual IPs/hostnames will differ; this is just illustrative.

---

## 5. Things to keep in mind

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Rate limits** | 4 requests per minute for free accounts, 60/min for paid. |
| **Pagination** | If more than 100 results, use `?page=2`, etc. |
| **Data freshness** | VirusTotal caches DNS data; the timestamp indicates when the last resolution was recorded. |
| **Privacy** | Do not share your API key publicly. |

---

## 6. Quick Python snippet

If you prefer Python, here’s a minimal example using `requests`:

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "api_key123"
DOMAIN = "yahoo.com"
URL = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/dns"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
    "Accept": "application/json"
}

response = requests.get(URL, headers=headers)
if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    print(data)
else:
    print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
```

---

### Recap

1. Hit `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com/dns` with your API key in the `x-apikey` header.  
2. Parse the JSON to see the list of IP addresses and hostnames that VirusTotal has recorded for that domain.  

Feel free to run the curl command or the Python script above, and you’ll get the DNS resolution data you’re looking for. If you hit any errors or need help interpreting the response, let me know!
